# 5. Interaction Flow

Based on the above functional architecture and the integration model of Agent/Copilot, this section focuses on how to enable end-to-end handling of service assurance scenarios, covering both single-domain autonomy and cross-domain coordination through the interaction and cooperation of agents at the Network layer and the Service layer.

## 5.1. Overall Interaction Flow

For L4 automation, the end-to-end private line service assurance process is depicted in the following figure.

[Figure: Figure 3 Overall interaction flow of enterprise PL service assurance]

There are three types of risk and fault resolution procedures. The first is a self-remediated process. Its interaction flow, shown sequentially as steps 1, 2, and 3a in Figure 3, illustrates this procedure. In this case, the Service Assurance Agent autonomously performs fault or risk detection, automated diagnostics, and self-repaired locally. Step 3a reports to the upper system aims for traceability and explainability. This forms a closed-loop operation entirely within the agent’s own domain.

As illustrated by steps 1, 2, 3b, and 4b” in Figure 3, the second type of interaction flow addresses issues whose resolution requires remote operations. In this case, the Service Assurance Agent in the Service Layer remotely instructs the Enterprise PL Service Assurance Agent in the Network Layer to execute all or part of the risk or fault resolution plan. Such operations may include, for example, replacing a faulty software module or restarting a stalled microservice instance.

The third type of risk and fault resolution, in contrast, requires on-site repair by the FME. The interaction flow is illustrated in Figure 3 as sequential steps 1, 2, 3b, 4b or 4b", 5b, and 6b. In this case, the Single-domain Service Assurance Agent combined with Cross-domain Service Assurance Agent autonomously detects faults or risks, performs automated diagnostics, and generates repair recommendations. If the recommendation requires network expansion, the agent invokes the network planning system to create the expansion plan and issue the work order to the FME (step 4b’). If no network expansion is required, the agent assigns the work order directly to the FME for on-site repair operations (step 4b). The FME then uses the Copilot to receive guided instructions for on-site operations (step 5b). Step 6b may be implemented through a natural language interface or integrated using an H5 plugin. In addition, NOC engineers may also utilize the NOC Copilot to proactively query specific service fault or risk information via natural language interaction, supporting efficient service operations and maintenance. This interaction flow is illustrated in Figure 3 as steps 4c and 5c.

## 5.2. Interface

The following table specifies the interfaces involved in steps 3a, 3b, 5c, and 6b as illustrated in Figure 3. These interfaces represent the primary points of interaction between the Service Layer and the Resource Layer.

**Table 7 Interfaces of steps 3a, 3b, 5c, and 6b in Figure 3**

| Step number | Interface Provider | Interface Consumer | Description of Network-side Functions with Open Interfaces | Interface ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [3a] Automatic reporting of closed-loop enterprise PL faults/risks | Enterprise PL Assurance Agent | Quality Assurance Center | Issue description, Auto-handling result | Network-EPL-Assurance-Agent-API-01 |
| [3b] Enterprise PL faults/risks requiring on-site repair or remote operation | Enterprise PL Assurance Agent | Quality Assurance Center | Issue description, Diagnostic result, Issue resolution recommendation | Network-EPL-Assurance-Agent-API-01 |
| [5c] Copilot Q&A interaction | Transport Network NOC Copilot | NOC Copilot | Intelligent Q&A messages | Network-FME-Copilot-API-01 |
| [6b] Copilot Q&A interaction | Transport Network FME Copilot | FME Copilot | Intelligent Q&A messages | Network-FME-Copilot-API-01 |

Note:

- Network-EPL-Assurance-Agent-API-01 is a machine-to-machine (i.e., agent-to-agent) interface which requires standardization. This interface provides the following functionalities:
  - Service Quality Issue Reporting: Initial reporting of a Service Quality-related fault or risk (Issue) to the upper-layer system
  - Service Quality Issue Update Reporting: Reports diagnostic results for intra-domain business faults/risks, including root cause identification, risk or fault localization, and suggested repair operations
  - Service Quality Issue Clearance Reporting: Reports the successful resolution or elimination of the Issue
  - Query Service Quality Issue List: Allows querying the list of current or historical o Service Quality Issues for tracking and analysis
